Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Now the Vikings get their biggest test yet. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Vikings vs. 49ers The Vikings are a different team with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. We saw last weekend that average quarterback play can turn a struggling, inept offense into a group that scores like an average NFL offense. It feels easy to take Minnesota again against San Francisco in Mexico City. However, I'm going to skip the side and total in favor of a prop. The 49ers rely on Christian McCaffrey as the workhorse of their offense, and that was on full display last weekend. He had 13 carries for just over 60 yards and added four catches for 161 yards. I'm targeting his receptions number in this game. The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. One way to combat that pressure is to get the running back out of the backfield quickly and find him on mismatches. We saw it last week when McCaffrey got matched up on Von Miller for a touchdown. I think the 49ers have to use McCaffrey in the passing game to have success against Minnesota's pressure. I like the Over on his receptions. Schwartz's Pick: Christian McCaffrey Over 4.5 receptions Buccaneers @ Lions This line could reflect Tampa Bay possibly being without quarterback Baker Mayfield, who is questionable with multiple injuries. However, I believe Mayfield will play, with the Bucs still in the hunt for a division title. He's a tough guy, and he won't miss this game. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Detroit's defense is without its two best players: Jack Campbell is unavailable, and star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured last week. The Lions' pass rush is significantly worse without Hutchinson, and any team, including the Bucs, will take advantage of it. No Lions lead will be safe moving forward. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover. After favorites wrecked Week 9, the underdogs got out to an early win. I have three early picks for primetime games in Germany, Cincinnati, and Baltimore. Best of luck and enjoy the weekend! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. Picks: Jared Goff Over 34.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Drake Maye Over 33.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Maye over 1.5 Pass TDs (1 unit) Chiefs (-3) at Falcons: O/U 47.5 No Kenneth Walker opens the door for Patrick Mahomes to have a day. The Falcons’ opponents have the ninth-highest pass rate over exception this season, and it’s third if you remove the Buccaneers game where Baker Mayfield threw three times in a monsoon. Atlanta is allowing 228.0 passing yards per game, but remove that Mayfield performance and the number rises to 271.3, which would rank last in the NFL. Here is the list of quarterbacks and how they’ve performed this season against Atlanta. Joe Burrow: 271 Baker Mayfield: 0 Brock Purdy: 288 Caleb Williams: 305 Tyler Huntley: 201 Tyler Shough: 286 Jordan Love: 312 Bryce Young: 287 Aaron Rodgers: 221 Six out of nine quarterbacks went over 240 passing yards, including three of the last four, and six of the past eight. Mahomes has thrown for at least 240 passing yards in five of eight games and two straight. Emmett Johnson has a surprising rushing prop of 71.5 and a rush + rec prop of 102.5, so he may get a heavy dosage, but in a dome setting, I think Kansas City reverts to trusting Mahomes more. I think he adds another to his resume in Atlanta. I’d go up to 244.5. This prop was 236.5 yesterday. Pick: Patrick Mahomes 240+ Passing Yards (1 unit) Jaguars (-10.5) at Titans: O/U 46.5 I lost on Tony Pollard ‘s under rushing yards last week against the Bengals, but will run it back on his Under. Pollard has 129 and 117 rushing yards in back-to-back games on 25 and 21 carries, plus five touchdowns. Both game scripts worked out that Tennessee was in the game until the final whistle, so running the ball was never out of the question. However, that could change here. Not only could the bye week throw off the ground game’s rhythm, but this matchup is the toughest of the season on paper. In the last three games, Derrick Henry was held to 57 rushing yards last week, and Jonathan Taylor to 23 yards two weeks ago, plus Woody Marks had 56 yards. New York has been competitive in consecutive divisional games and has extra rest after playing Thursday, and Jacksonville is traveling for a second consecutive road game. Despite those stat lines, both New York players are worth fading in this week's matchup. The Jaguars have been stout against the run and are defending tight ends at a high level. The defense allows only 67.4 rushing yards per game to opposing running backs, the third-lowest mark in the NFL. The additions of defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux will boost the run defense even more. Jacksonville is also allowing a league-low 31.0 receiving yards per game to tight ends. So, let's take the under on both Skattebo and Likely's yardage props. Likely has 50+ receiving yards in five of his last six games, while Skattebo has 55+ rushing yards in five of his past six games as well. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images My early Week 11 NFL player props start with two running backs coming off very different Sundays James Cook broke a 74-yard run for Buffalo, while Christian McCaffrey did most of his damage as a receiver See my three Week 11 NFL prop picks and projected lines below James Cook ran for 157 yards against the Jets. Christian McCaffrey had 161 yards receiving against Dallas. Both performances will draw attention to their Week 11 NFL player props, but I’d approach their rushing totals very differently. Last week, two of my three early targets cleared their projected lines. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 171 receiving yards and Ja’Marr Chase caught 11 passes. McCaffrey fell three rushing yards short, even as he scored three touchdowns. Cook gets Miami in Buffalo, McCaffrey faces Minnesota in Mexico City and Chase visits Washington on Monday night. Even his best game, a 75-yard afternoon against Arizona, would have beaten my projected line by just half a yard. McCaffrey has had seven, 18 and 13 carries in his last three games. Las Vegas was the one opponent in that stretch against whom he got a steady afternoon of handoffs. He finished with 68 yards. Dallas gave up 161 receiving yards to McCaffrey on just four catches. I want his rushing under if the line opens in the mid-70s: he can hurt Minnesota on a screen or a wheel route without adding a yard to his rushing total. Minnesota has allowed 4.2 yards per carry on 241 attempts. The workload I’d worry about is 18 or 19 carries. At 13, the number he got in Dallas, he’d need a gain of nearly six yards per attempt to beat me. My cutoff matters here. If the opening line lands near the 62 yards he put up in Dallas, I’d pass. In the mid-70s, I’m happy to let his receiving yards grab the headlines. He’s rushed for at least 90 yards in six of nine games, including five of the six in which Buffalo gave him 20 or more carries. Cook has 344 rushing yards on 70 attempts over his last three games. His other 17 carries went for 83, seven short of what I’m looking for against the Dolphins. The Minnesota game is why I don’t need a repeat of that highlight. Cook’s longest run against the Vikings went for 11 yards. He still finished with 107 because Buffalo went back to him 31 times. Miami has allowed 1,066 rushing yards on 270 attempts, 4.0 per carry, without giving up a run longer than 27 yards in that sample. Teams have kept running on them, which suits how Cook piles up yardage. If Buffalo falls behind and has to throw, the cushion disappears. Cook had just 57 yards on 13 carries in Houston and 75 on 12 against New England. I’m backing him to get closer to his usual workload at home. Early Bet: James Cook over 89.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #3: Ja’Marr Chase Receptions For Ja’Marr Chase’s receptions prop against Washington, I’m looking at how quickly Cincinnati’s passing game has shifted. Chase caught 32 passes in his last three games. It took all six of his previous games combined to catch that many. He went for 11 catches against Tennessee, 10 against Atlanta and 11 against Pittsburgh. He’s reached eight in four of nine games overall, so this pick depends on Cincinnati continuing to feed him the way it has over the last three games. The Pittsburgh highlight is the 231 receiving yards. For NFL total receptions props , I give the Atlanta game just as much weight. Chase cleared this target by two catches there without needing anything close to 231 yards. Washington has allowed 217 receptions for 2,341 receiving yards to all positions this season. That total includes backs and tight ends, so it tells us what opponents have done through the air, not which receiver will get the ball. Eight catches is where I’d draw the line for Chase. I’d play the over at 7.5 on Monday night. At 8.5, the price of admission becomes a ninth catch, something Chase managed just once in those first six games. That’s where I’d stop.
